label: prop:level-selection-not-linear
title: Linear level-selection is excluded (exponential beats linear)
html:
Let w = w_{\mathrm{std}} be the branched brane-tower weight, which by Brane-tower growth above the containment threshold (GAP-A-3) satisfies c\,r^{k} \leq w(k) for k \geq 3 with r = \sqrt{2} > 1 and c = 1/30 > 0. If the binding is extensive — w(A) \leq M \cdot A for every A \geq 1 — then a contradiction follows. Consequently no linear level-selection rule k(A) = A (nor bond-count k(A) = A(A-1)/2, a fortiori) is consistent with extensive binding: the selected jet level grows at most logarithmically in A.

Proof idea. The tower bound gives c\,r^{A} \leq w(A) \leq M\cdot A for all A \geq 1. But a geometric c\,r^{A} with r > 1 eventually outgrows any linear M\cdot A — formally (A) = o(r^{A}) as A \to \infty — so the inequality cannot hold for all A. Dividing the surviving bound by c and taking \log_r shows k(A) \leq \log_r\!\big((M/c)\,A\big), i.e. at most logarithmic growth.

Restriction of the hypothesis to A \geq 1. Extensivity is imposed only for A \geq 1, the physical regime. Excluding A = 0 ensures the exclusion is the genuine growth argument rather than a degenerate boundary coincidence: at A = 0 the linear side is M \cdot 0 = 0, so the inequality would fail or hold for reasons unrelated to the exponential-versus-linear mechanism.

The tower bound does not force w(0) \geq c > 0: w_{\mathrm{std}}(0) = 0, because no diagram of fewer than three cells contains (2,1). Stated for every k, the growth hypothesis would be false at k = 0, so the A = 0 case is a falsity in the antecedent rather than a boundary effect in the conclusion. That is why Brane-tower growth above the containment threshold (GAP-A-3) now carries a threshold, and why this proposition is unconditional rather than conditional.
